MCS_use_definitions.description: Long-term use of MCS (LVAD) as an alternative to transplantation in patients with end-stage heart failure (HF) ineligible for transplantation.

MCS_use_definitions.strategy: Bridge to decision (BTD) / Bridge to bridge (BTB)
MCS_use_definitions.description: Use of short-term MCS (e.g., ECMO or Impella) in patients with cardiogenic shock until hemodynamics and end-organ perfusion are stabilized, contraindications for long-term MCS are excluded and additional therapeutic options (including long-term VAD therapy or heart transplant) can be evaluated.
Use of MCS (usually LVAD) to improve end-organ function and/or to make an initially ineligible patient eligible for heart transplantation.
Use of MCS (LVAD, BiVAD or TAH) to keep a patient alive who is at high risk of death before transplantation until a donor organ becomes available.
Use of MCS (short-term or long-term) to keep a patient alive until cardiac function recovers sufficiently to remove MCS.

content.INTERMACS_recommendation: Long-term MCS should be considered in patients with INTERMACS profiles 2 to 4, and in some patients with INTERMACS profile 5 (and 6 when high-risk characteristics are present). Patients without irreversible end‑organ failure other than cardiac, or recovering from INTERMACS level 1 while on short-term MCS, may also qualify for long-term MCS.
content.Table_16_title: Patients potentially eligible for implantation of a left ventricular assist device (LVAD)
content.Table_16_overview: Patients with persistent severe symptoms despite optimal medical and device therapy, without severe right ventricular dysfunction and/or severe tricuspid regurgitation, with a stable psychosocial background and absence of major contraindications, and who have at least one of the listed criteria.
Table_16_specific_criteria: LVEF < 25% and unable to exercise for HF or, if able to perform cardiopulmonary exercise testing, peak VO2 < 12 mL/kg/min and/or < 50% predicted value.
≥ 3 HF hospitalizations in the previous 12 months without an obvious precipitating cause.
Dependence on intravenous inotropic therapy or temporary MCS.

Progressive end-organ dysfunction (worsening renal and/or hepatic function, type II pulmonary hypertension, cardiac cachexia) due to reduced perfusion and not to inadequately low ventricular filling pressure (examples noted in guideline: PCWP ≥ 20 mmHg, SBP ≤ 90 mmHg or cardiac index ≤ 2 L/min/m²).
